props.caption: Flip V: turns the picture upside down, top to bottom
props.title: Building the Reflection

B19.capture_spec: C09: capture_scenes.gd id C09 (pond; Reflection is a plain flipped copy, no material, modulate alpha 0 to 1 over 2.0 to 3.0 s; Player static at x 520); 11 s, 30 fps, Forward+, scripted.
B19.visual_intent: Act title 'Building the Reflection' (serif 40) top-left. The real pond with the blob standing on the shoreline. At about 2 s a flipped copy of the blob fades in right under its feet (the copy has no shader yet); a terracotta ring marks where the feet meet the copy and a label 'Flip V' lands beside the copy.
B19.motion_claim: A flipped copy fades in directly under the feet.

show.event: blob on the shore, no copy
ring where feet meet the copy

B19.runner_up: manim drawing of a blob and its mirror image
B19.why: The viewer sees the real node settings' result: the same picture, flipped and placed, exactly as the Inspector would produce it.

B20.visual_intent: A small scene-tree diagram: 'Player' (teal blob icon) with a child chip 'RemoteTransform2D'; a separate branch 'Reflection' (a flipped blob icon); a dashed line from the chip to the Reflection node. Under the diagram, a strip of shoreline: the blob slides right along it and the flipped blob under it follows in lockstep while the dashed line pulses each time. A label from the docs: 'pushes its transform to another node'.
B20.motion_claim: The blob slides right and the flipped blob under it follows in lockstep, the dashed line pulsing.

show.event: tree diagram: Player, RemoteTransform2D, separate Reflection branch
dashed line drawn from the chip to Reflection
blob slides; the flipped blob follows

B20.why: The claim is 'follows without being its child'; two separate branches with a moving pair show exactly that.

B21.capture_spec: C10: capture_scenes.gd id C10 (pond; Reflection plain flipped sprite, no material; Player walks x 300 to 1000 over 10.5 s); 11.5 s, 30 fps, Forward+, scripted walk.
B21.visual_intent: The real pond with the plain flipped copy following the blob along the shoreline: over the open water it looks right, but when the blob passes the sandbar the copy is drawn right over the sand. Readouts 'no map yet' then 'in the sand'; one terracotta ring on the copy over the sand.
B21.motion_claim: The copy slides over the sandbar and stays visible on the sand.

show.event: readout 'no map yet'; copy over water
ring on the copy over the sand

B21.why: The failure is easiest to feel as the real mistake happening: a flipped copy sitting on dry sand.

B22.visual_intent: Two linked panels of the pond: left 'the screen' with a terracotta dot on one pixel of the reflection, right 'the copy' (the red and green map) with its twin dot at the same place; a dashed link between the dots and the tag 'screen UV: the same address in both'. The dot moves along the reflection and its twin moves with it; the colour under the twin changes the small label from 'water' to 'sand' as the dot crosses onto the sandbar. A label 'screen UV: a pixel's address on the whole screen'.
B22.motion_claim: The dot on the reflection moves and its twin on the map moves with it; the label under the twin turns from 'water' to 'sand'.
B22.why: The same address in two pictures is a correspondence; two linked panels with moving twin dots show it.

cues.label: SCREEN_UV: a pixel's address on the whole screen
distance: how far apart two colors are
alpha: how visible a pixel is: 0 invisible, 1 solid

B23.capture_spec: C11: capture_scenes.gd id C11 (pond; shader lab-shaders/02-reflection.gdshader; Player walks x 300 to 1000 over 11.5 s); 12.5 s, 30 fps, Forward+, scripted walk.
B23.visual_intent: Code card at left (the ten-line reflection shader); at right the real pond with the shader on the reflection: the blob walks, the reflection shows over water and is gone over the sandbar. The lines light up as the voice reads: the lookup line, the water test, the alpha line. Readouts 'keep' over water and 'alpha zero' near the sandbar.
B23.motion_claim: The lookup, test and alpha lines light up in turn while the reflection shows over water and vanishes over the sand.
B23.why: The three lines are the whole effect; the real result next to them, and the lines lighting with the voice, is the claim.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · scripted (the Label Map node is switched at run time)

B24.capture_spec: C12: capture_scenes.gd id C12 (pond; shader 02; Player walks x 180 to 620 over 12.5 s over open water; LabelMap.visible false from 4.5 s to 9.5 s); 13 s, 30 fps, Forward+, scripted.
B24.visual_intent: The real pond with the blob walking over open water. At 4.5 s the LabelMap node is switched off: the picture does not change except that the reflection disappears. At 9.5 s it is switched on again and the reflection returns. Readouts 'Map on', 'Map off', 'Map on'.
B24.motion_claim: The reflection vanishes and returns as the LabelMap node is switched off and on, and nothing else in the picture changes.

show.event: readout 'Map off'; reflection gone, picture otherwise identical

B24.runner_up: manim drawing of two frames and what differs between them
B24.why: A real switch with an identical rest of the picture is the evidence; a drawing could only claim it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · scripted (the order is changed in the tree at run time)

B25.capture_spec: C13: capture_scenes.gd id C13 (pond; shader 02; Player walks x 300 to 560; move_child(BackBufferCopy, Ground's index) at 4.0 s; move_child(LabelMap, Ground's index) at 9.5 s); 13.5 s, 30 fps, Forward+, scripted.
B25.visual_intent: The real pond. State one: map, copy, art (the reflection shows). At 4 s the copy node is moved after the art: the reflection disappears and nothing else changes. At 9.5 s the LabelMap is moved over the art: a red and green sea covers the pond and the reflection is back. Readouts show the order ('map · copy · art', 'map · art · copy', 'art · map · copy') and the outcome ('reflection', 'no reflection', 'red sea').
B25.motion_claim: The reflection disappears when the copy moves after the art; a red sea covers the pond when the map moves over it.

show.event: order map, copy, art; reflection shows
order map, art, copy; no reflection
order art, map, copy; red sea, reflection back

B25.runner_up: manim stack with the copy frame moving
B25.why: Two real failures, one after the other in one scene, show what each wrong order looks like to the person debugging it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · scripted (the art's opacity is changed at run time)

B26.capture_spec: C14: capture_scenes.gd id C14 (pond; shader 02; Ground modulate alpha 1.0, eased to 0.9 over 3.0 to 4.0 s, back to 1.0 at 9.5 s); 13 s, 30 fps, Forward+, scripted. The stage colour shows through the art at 0.9, so the whole picture lightens a little: expected.
B26.visual_intent: The real pond. At 3 s the art layer's opacity eases from 100 to 90 percent: the water turns a faint periwinkle and a pale green ring shows around the sandbar, the map leaking through. At 9.5 s it returns to 100 percent and the leak is gone. Readouts 'art 100%', 'art 90%', 'art 100%'; a terracotta ring on the leaking green ring while it shows.
B26.motion_claim: A faint purple tint and a green ring appear when the art drops to ninety percent and disappear when it returns to full.

show.event: ring on the leaking green ring

B26.runner_up: manim drawing of an overlay with alpha
B26.why: The leak is a visible change in a real frame, with the exact opacity labelled; the viewer sees how little transparency is enough.
